name: AKS Kubernetes Event Deletion
description: Kubernetes records important cluster events — crashes, deployments, permission changes — so operators can see what happened. On AKS, an attacker with rights to delete those events is wiping the cluster's short-term memory. The workloads may still be running a backdoor; you just cannot see the breadcrumb. Event deletion is almost never a normal admin task. Treat it as covering tracks.
mitigations: Rotate credentials if the actor is compromised
